Script interpreters like python3, perl, and php run any script you give them.
Allowlisting the interpreter (like Python or PHP) itself means every new script it
runs inherits the interpreter's permissions, including all the scripts
you never reviewed. One approval ends up covering far more than you saw.
Secure Script Launchers are small programs that sit in front of the real
interpreter, identify which script is being run, and apply that script's
Each interpreter is routed through its Secure Script Launcher. After
activation, scripts are reviewed on their own permission terms.
Interpreters without a launcher (bash, sh) are handled in the Programs queue.
